links.outcome: Consistency of LLM conclusions across equivalent questions differing in framing and language style
links.effect: Positive vs negative framed pairs significantly more likely to yield contradictory conclusions than same-framing pairs; amplified in multi-turn conversations; no significant framing by language-style interaction.
links.quote: Our findings show that positively- and negatively-framed pairs are significantly more likely to produce contradictory conclusions than same-framing pairs.

links.outcome: Response consistency under paraphrased or reframed medical questions with identical evidence
links.effect: Opposite-framing query pairs were significantly more likely to produce contradictory conclusions across eight LLMs; inconsistency increased with sustained persuasion in multi-turn conversations.
links.quote: Our findings show that positively- and negatively-framed pairs are significantly more likely to produce contradictory conclusions than same-framing pairs.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating phrasing robustness of RAG-based medical QA using expert-selected evidence documents

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM robustness to query framing and phrasing bias in a medical Q&A benchmark setting without testing an organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
